definition: In natural language processing, IOB tagging (abbreviation for Inside–outside–beginning) (or BIO tagging) is a common format for tagging tokens in a chunking task.
details: IOB stands for "inside, outside, beginning". It was proposed in 1995.

explainer.lead: IOB tagging is a common format for tagging tokens in chunking tasks in natural language processing. It was proposed in 1995.

tiers.eli5: Each word gets a label saying whether it starts a chunk, continues one, or sits outside any chunk.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it to mark token spans for chunking, with tags for inside, outside and beginning. No specific pitfall is given in the supplied facts.
tiers.paperLevel: IOB stands for inside, outside, beginning; it is a format for tagging tokens in a chunking task. Proposed in 1995.

explainer.example: In a chunking task, each token in a sentence receives an I, O or B tag indicating its role in a chunk.
